Team —

Attaching the March monthly metrics extract and an early draft of the QBR readout (attachments). High level asks ahead of Friday's leadership prep:

1) Ownership confirmation: who will own the latency remediation story (95p/median gap) for the next sprint? I want a named owner and a short remediation plan by EOD Thursday.

2) Cost-to-throughput tradeoffs: Jonas, please call out 2 levered options (batching profile change + quantized variant rollout) and the expected unit-cost delta for the top 3 busiest routes.

3) Uptime narrative: there was a 45-minute degradation on 3/05 tied to autoscaler churn — we need the incident summary (root cause + mitigation) for the QBR appendix. Naomi, can you consolidate the incident timeline and add a one-slide corrective action?

4) Usage signals: Laura, please highlight any account-level usage surge that looks anomalous (>=3x baseline) and whether prefix caching would have reduced cost. If Acme's March burst is real, call it out.

Actions & deadlines:
- Named owners and short bullets (Vivek inbox) — Thu 3/19 11:59 PDT
- Jonas cost options, rough numbers — Thu 3/19 17:00 PDT
- Naomi incident timeline slide — Thu 3/19 12:00 PDT
- Laura account anomalies and recommended cache flags — Thu 3/19 15:00 PDT

I linked the working drive folder and the JIRA ticket for backlog items (related_links). We'll walk the readout in the prep on Friday. Keep the replies short — if you hit blockers ping me on Slack (ops-performance).

Thanks —
Vivek

Vivek —

Thanks. Quick read of the metrics: top 3 routes by token volume are /chat/generate, /embed/vectorize, /summarize/doc. Initial notes:

- Option A (conservative): increase batching window from 12ms -> 20ms for /embed/vectorize only, estimate ~12% unit cost reduction for that route, 2–5ms p95 increase for chat. No model change, low risk.
- Option B (aggressive): enable int8 quantized variant for embed model in dedicated pools during off-peak; ~28% unit-cost reduction for embed, risk: mild quality delta for long-tail prompts, requires canary and rollback plan.

I'll run quick back-of-envelope numbers and drop a spreadsheet to the Drive by Thu EOD (link in related_links). Owner for the latency remediation: I'm willing to take the lead on the batching experiment and coordinate with infra to measure p95 before/after.

Action: Jonas -> lead batching experiment (start 3/22), report progress in ops standup.

Jonas

Vivek / team —

Attached is a compact incident timeline and a one-slide corrective-action summary for the QBR appendix. Root cause in short: autoscaler mis-evaluated GPU utilization under short-burst traffic patterns due to a stale utilization smoothing parameter; that triggered a scale-down that raced with scheduled batch flushes. Mitigations proposed:

- Immediate: adjust smoothing window to reduce sensitivity to sub-1m bursts (config change) — ops rollout 3/20
- Near term: add a guard to prevent concurrent scale-down during batch flush windows (infra/TTC) — Jira INF-1245
- Monitoring: add an SLI breakpoint alert at 5m degradation to trigger on-call earlier

I've attached service-uptime-incident-log.csv and a single-slide summary in the Drive. I'm also flagging a related gap: we have no automatic canary for autoscaler config changes — recommend we add a small canary policy before autoscaler tuning.

Naomi
Head of Reliability
[Attachment: service-uptime-incident-log.csv (csv, 48KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference service readiness & OKR check — QBR prep

Vivek / team —

Checked account-level traffic: Acme Analytics generated a sustained 3.7x increase for /embed/vectorize between 03/02–03/06, consistent with a data-science batch they started. I verified the request pattern (large-batch single-caller) — prefix caching wouldn't have helped much because payloads were distinct.

Recommendations:
- Short term: rate-limit per-account batch concurrency for public routes to protect shared pools (quick config, low risk).
- Medium term: offer a dedicated reserved flow for high-volume analytics customers (sales/partner pathway).

I'm tagging procurement and Acme's contact (anna.li@acme-analytics.com) to discuss a reserved capacity pilot. I'll draft a 1-paragraph outreach and share it to the Drive by EOD.

Laura
Head of Customer Success
